clause_added: A second except clause, except publisher.PublishRefused, after the except NotYetAvailable clause around the reader call appends the client id to out["refused"] and continues to the next client.
words: run_filled_report now catches publisher.PublishRefused raised by the reader (a household the reader cannot compose, such as a duplicated household-grain member, a missing window or a missing first data date), records the client in out["refused"] and goes on to the next client, as it already did for a document the publisher refuses at publish. Before this change the reader's refusal escaped the pass, so once the switch is on one such household would end the whole run. NotYetAvailable still records not_available, any other exception still propagates, and the switch off still reads and writes nothing. Three tests whose names carry reader_refused were added to test_filled_report_publish.py; the two filled-report test files pass 38 of 38 under pytest. NOT PROVEN: nothing was deployed or run against AWS, the switch stays off, no real household was exercised, and the reader's household id-space match with the directory is unmeasured.
